profile.headline: Senior Principal Software Engineer
profile.summary:
I am a Senior Principal Software Engineer and technical leader who bridges the gap between tactical-edge operational needs and enterprise-scale architectures. My career began in the U.S. Army and evolved into leading technology deployments in Afghanistan for DARPA, which ingrained in me a deep empathy for the end-user and the critical importance of reliable, mission-driven systems.

Today, I direct complex technical efforts and lead large cross-functional teams to deliver software for both prototype efforts and defense Programs of Record (PORs). I specialize in envisioning, architecting, and delivering emerging technologies to satisfy real-world user requirements. From orchestrating agentic workflows to modernizing legacy infrastructure into scalable Kubernetes deployments, my focus is always on turning rapid prototypes into "real," hardened software relied upon by an active, operational user base.

Beyond the code, I am driven by strategic business outcomes and team culture. Whether spearheading multi-provider integrations with partners like Anduril, Palantir, and Systematic, or navigating complex program milestones, I believe the best technical solutions come from teams built on psychological safety, clear communication, and continuous mentorship.

Outside of my primary leadership responsibilities, I am a relentless tinkerer who maintains a private, self-hosted infrastructure. I rapidly prototype custom software and automation solutions, explore the application of the latest AI advances, and remain actively hands-on in the codebase to aggressively contribute features and remediate defects. I thrive on solving complex challenges and standardizing workflows that empower my organization to unlock new levels of success.

Clearance: Current US Government Security Clearance

positions.title: Senior Principal Software Engineer
positions.description:
- Led critical infrastructure modernizations, including an internal migration from Jenkins and Docker to GitLab and Kubernetes, and architected secure CI/CD pipelines with DevSecOps integration.

- Spearheaded the enterprise shift to an AI-Driven Development Lifecycle (AIDLC) by authoring and presenting a 50-page strategic implementation plan to senior leadership. Currently executing this spec-driven architecture, integrating LLMs and agentic orchestration to fundamentally accelerate engineering velocity.

- Rapidly designed and delivered technical interoperability and strategic partnership foundations for a one-way effector integration.

- Steered the technical execution of a joint, multi-organizational program as the primary Development Lead and technical anchor directly under the overall Tech Lead. Acted as a versatile technical catalyst—balancing cross-functional sprint execution with hands-on prototyping, advanced system design, and comprehensive team mentorship to bridge the gap between systems engineering, testing, and software development.

positions.title: Principal Software Engineer
positions.description:
- Served as the overall Technical Lead for a large, complex enterprise software program, directing the technical execution of three concurrent task orders representing tens of millions in contract value.

- Supervised subordinate development team leads and coordinated a cross-functional engineering organization of dozens of personnel, overseeing the end-to-end translation of complex military requirements into operational software.

- Forged high-trust, collaborative relationships with government leadership to clarify scope and navigate programmatic ambiguity. Successfully protected team morale and maintained consistent delivery velocity despite staffing reductions and complex contract transitions. 

- Architected and led the deployment of of a new, secure CI/CD pipeline with DevSecOps integration within a strict government AWS cloud environment

positions.title: Senior Software Engineer
positions.description:
- Led a development team executing full stack software engineering for a Program of Record, mentoring engineers and guiding the design of scalable enterprise solutions.

- Architected robust Extract, Transform, Load (ETL) systems integration solutions using Apache NiFi, alongside developing React-based web components and Java Spring Boot microservices.

- Designed and created a novel Java-based anomaly detection library implementing Local Outlier Factor (LOF) and Interquartile Range (IQR) algorithms specifically optimized for Android tactical devices.

- Authored the Past Performance volume for a major contract proposal, engineering a custom Natural Language Processing (NLP) prototype to align our submission exactly with RFP language, which secured the maximum allowable evaluation credit.

positions.title: Product Owner/Afghanistan Operations Manager
positions.description:
- Directed product strategy as a Product Owner for the DARPA TransApps program, shaping development priorities, driving the long-term roadmap, and orchestrating multiple software releases within a complex, multi-stakeholder ecosystem.

- Authorized the final release and fielding of mobile technology to warfighters in active combat operations, ensuring all software met stringent tactical and reliability standards.

- Managed Afghanistan operations and led a deployed FSR team supporting 2,000+ users, driving the strategic expansion of the program by engaging and advising stakeholders ranging from tactical commanders to Division commanders, ISAF staff, and Senior Executive Service (SES) personnel.

- Authored multiple tactical applications that successfully transitioned to follow-on Army Programs of Record, having independently taught myself Android development during spare time in austere deployed conditions.

positions.title: Lead Field Support Representative
positions.description:
- Managed the fielding and tactical application of the DARPA Tactical Ground Reporting (TIGR) system across southern Afghanistan.

- Supervised and trained FSRs, ensuring continuous operational readiness of synchronized server/client intelligence architectures in degraded network environments.

- Worked closely with tactical end-users to discover novel operational use cases and train them on applying TIGR to their specific mission sets.

- Bridged the gap between the field and the lab by identifying capability gaps, documenting complex requirements, and translating user needs directly to DARPA engineering teams to drive future development.

positions.title: Captain
positions.description:
- Served 16 years across the USAR, Regular Army, and IRR, advancing from Private to Captain.

- Deployed in support of Operation Iraqi Freedom (OIF 2005-2006, 2008-2009) and Operation Bright Star.

- Specialized in Logistics and Civil Affairs, building a foundational expertise in tactical operations, supply chain management, and cross-cultural leadership.

honors.title: Winner of RII's October 2019 Raspberry Pi Project Competition
honors.description:
I teamed up with good friend Aaron Lubben to develop a unique prototype capability. Our winning project combined computer vision, machine learning, and existing military systems to populate a Common Operating Picture (COP, or military commander's map view) with MIL-STD-2525c symbols based on what the cameras and program detected - in real time.

We used OpenCV in conjunction with other frameworks such as YOLOv3, Tensorflow, and Keras when writing the project software. Our software, using object detection, transforms items of interest embedded inside live video frames into data objects that can be more easily shared, persisted, analyzed, and can contribute to additional AI/ML predictions. 

For our demonstration we incorporated several live camera feeds. Two feeds were from streaming cameras found online (a traffic camera for a small town in Ohio, a view of the Venice canals). We also set up a live streaming video feed using a Raspberry Pi to monitor activity outside our office building. As our audience viewed the cameras, they could simultaneously view real-time position location updates on our tactical maps matching the activity seen in the video feeds. 

Winning this competition included a cash award.
honors.issuer: Issued by Research Innovations Inc. · Oct 2019

projects.title: The Llama Library
projects.description:
Options for performing anomaly detection in Android with lightweight frameworks are currently limited. The best anomaly detection libraries are written in Python or other languages that are difficult to use or incompatible with Android applications and services. Existing Java-based libraries primarily target enterprise applications. 

To solve this problem I wrote a library in Java implementing the Local Outlier Factor (LOF) algorithm as well as the simpler Interquartile Range (IQR) algorithm. The library allows Android (or other Java-based applications) developers to perform anomaly detection as part of their application or service. Training, saving the training results, and sharing the trained model is easy. Evaluating new data to detect either anomalies or clustered data is fast and efficient.

projects.title: Remote Capture of Vital Signs
projects.description:
This is a personal project I submitted to our company's Pi Day competition in March, where employees compete to see whose Raspberry Pi project earns top honors. I teamed up with good friend and coworker Aaron Lubben to combine one Raspberry Pi board with a Texas Instruments  millimeter wave sensor development board.

Using these paired devices, we are able to use millimeter wave technology to monitor a person's pulse and breathing rate (without anything touching the person). We have integrated our boards with other systems to wirelessly send the vital signs data as part of a position location information update message, so that military commanders could monitor their respective Soldiers' health status as a part of their Common Operating Picture (COP).
